incident-bot: [P1] Smart-routing + fallback policy failure: dedicated tenants routed to hosted pool -> wrong model-variant + cross-region retry loop detected. Auto-paging oncall.
incident-bot: Symptoms: 502/503 spikes for dedicated customers, unexpected model variant (small-fp16) used for dedicated workloads, retry churn between us-west-2 <-> ap-southeast-1.
Liam (oncall): Acknowledged page. Jumping in. Which tenants impacted? Customer-visible severity?
Olivia (support): Two escalations in live chat: acct-1102 (HealthCo) and acct-2203 (RetailOps). Both report degraded output quality and intermittent errors. Ticket 9104 opened.
Maya (SRE): Pulling routing traces and policy evaluations. Found a window at 03:07:12 UTC where policy engine selected `hosted_pool` for requests with header `X-Tier: dedicated`. Policy decision print: `chosen_rule: availability-first (priority=90)`. Dedicated bind rule `bind-dedicated` has priority 80. So availability-first won.
Noah (runtime): availability-first rule looks new from this morning's rollout. Its match clause is loose: `match: tenant.flags.tier_preference != null`. Some tenants got `tier_override=true` from billing-sync and that satisfied the match.
Maya (SRE): Cross-region loop: hosted pool attempts us-west-2 -> if capacity low then failover to ap-southeast-1; but client-side retry immediately retries to us-west-2 causing back-and-forth and amplified load. See snippet from router logs:
```
[03:07:12] req id=abcd1234 tenant=acct-1102 match=availability-first -> route=hosted_pool us-west-2 variant=small-fp16
[03:07:13] req id=abcd1234 routed_to=ap-southeast-1 retry=1 err=503
[03:07:14] req id=abcd1234 retry_to=us-west-2 err=502
```
Olivia (support): HealthCo says hallucinations increased; they specifically called out summary outputs missing sections. They were on a demo call. 
Priya (CS): I'm on a call with HealthCo now. They want a root cause and ETA.
Liam (oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) emergency lock to route dedicated tenants to dedicated pool (high priority rule). 2) pause billing-sync to avoid more `tier_override` writes. 3) temporarily disable cross-region fallback to stop churn. Maya, run step 1. Noah, do step 3.
Maya (SRE): Applying emergency override: 
`controlctl policy add --policy smart-routing --rule '{"id":"dedicated-lock-emergency","match":"tenant.flags.tier == \"dedicated\"","action":"route_to: dedicated_pool","priority":999}'`
deploy-bot: policy smart-routing patched (patch id: emg-279999).
Maya (SRE): Observed routing change within 10s: acct-1102/2203 now routed to dedicated_pool. Error rate dropping for those tenants.
Noah (runtime): Pausing fallback: `kubectl -n runtime patch configmap fallback-config -p '{"data":{"cross_region_fallback":"false"}}'` -> change applied. This should stop region bouncing.
Maya (SRE): Pausing billing-sync job to prevent additional bad flags: `kubectl -n infra rollout pause job/billing-sync` -> paused.
Liam (oncall): Good. Next: revert hosted pool default model-variant if it differs from dedicated expectations. What variant hit them?
Maya (SRE): Logs show hosted default variant = `small-fp16-experimental`. Dedicated expected `large-accurate-v1`. We should not rely on hosted defaults for dedicated traffic anyway, but because of misroute this caused quality regression.
Noah (runtime): Temporarily set hosted pool default to `small-robust-v1` to reduce hallucination risk: `modelctl set-default --pool hosted_pool --variant small-robust-v1` -> applied.
Priya (CS): Sending immediate note to HealthCo and RetailOps with mitigation and apology. Draft link: https://git.internal/cs/drafts/2799998888.
Olivia (support): Both customers acknowledged the note; HealthCo requested incident call recording and will consider SLA credit.
Maya (SRE): Running scan to find tenants with `tier_override=true`: `redis-cli --scan --pattern tenant:* | xargs -n1 sh -c "redis-cli HGETALL $0 | grep tier_override"` -> found 14 tenants. Cleaning up overrides for those marked enterprise: `redis-cli HSET tenant:acct-1102 tier_override false` etc. Scripted patch in progress.
Noah (runtime): Adding defensive validation to policy compiler: any `match` containing `tier_preference` must not match if tenant has `is_enterprise=true` unless explicit. Opening PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/controlplane/pull/678
Maya (SRE): Root cause summary so far: billing-sync wrote `tier_override=true` for some dedicated tenants due to missing enterprise tag mapping in its v2 rollout. availability-first policy (rolled earlier) matched those flags and had higher priority than bind-dedicated. Result: misrouting to hosted pool and wrong model variant; cross-region fallback caused retry storm.
Liam (oncall): Handoff plan: I'll stay for 20m then hand to Maya for post-incident. Create INC-279999 ticket and attach timeline. Maya, you'll own postmortem and customer impact calc.
Priya (CS): I'll lead customer comms and coordinate SLA credit calculation with finance.
Olivia (support): Support will monitor tickets 9104 and 9105 and be on standby for calls.
Maya (SRE): Post-mitigation tasks: 1) Revert bad billing-sync commit & roll forward fixed job. 2) Remove emergency rule after 2h stable and re-evaluate policy priorities. 3) Audit model-registry pool defaults and pin dedicated tenancy mapping. 4) Add monitoring alert for policy-override events (when availability-first fires for `tenant.flags.tier`).
Liam (oncall): Timeline note: 03:00 rollout billing-sync-v2 -> 03:06 availability-first rollout -> 03:07 misroutes spike -> 03:09 alert -> 03:11 emergency rule applied -> 03:15 fallback disabled & billing-sync paused -> 03:25 hosted default swapped -> 03:40 cleanup started -> 04:00 stability checks green so far.
incident-bot: Incident INC-279999 created. State: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem owners: Maya (SRE), Noah (runtime), Billing-sync owner (infra).
Liam (oncall): reactions :rotating_light: :shield: :white_check_mark:. Leaving channel; handoff to Maya.
